alternatives_considered: Treating each reported NAPCS product as a separate operating market was rejected because the NAICS definition excludes establishments providing only one support service and industry-product relationships do not establish operating-boundary centrality.
Adopting narrow prior seeds was rejected because the frozen pack provides no operating-model evidence that any seed defines the bundled office-administration boundary.
analysis_summary: The bounded family resolves to one provisional-quality but usable operating market: contracted, bundled day-to-day office administration for other organizations, excluding complete operation of a client business and standalone specialist services. The NAICS definition directly supports the bundled-service boundary; the reported NAPCS identities are products observed as sold by the industry, not proof of separate market membership. All retrieved prior candidates lack sufficient frozen evidence to establish equivalence to this operating boundary.

proposed_markets.acquisition_universe: Providers whose primary offering is a contract or fee-based bundle of recurring day-to-day office administrative services for other organizations; exclude providers selling only one specialist support service or operating the client's complete business.
proposed_markets.ambient_ai_workflow: AI can assist recordkeeping, billing workflows, personnel administration, routing, and document handling, but the market boundary remains accountable delivery of the bundled administrative service rather than sale of AI software.
proposed_markets.boundary: Includes externally provided, bundled day-to-day financial-planning, billing and recordkeeping, personnel, and physical-distribution/logistics administration. Excludes complete operation of a client business, internal corporate managing offices, consulting without day-to-day management, property management, facilities management, staffing, and standalone specialist services such as accounting, payroll, tax, mail, document, IT, or legal support.
proposed_markets.buyer: Organizations that contract an outside provider to run a range of their day-to-day office administrative functions.
proposed_markets.definition: A market for providers that deliver a bundled range of day-to-day office administrative functions for other organizations on a contract or fee basis, without providing the operating staff required to run the client's complete business.
proposed_markets.delivery_model: Recurring contracted or fee-based managed administrative delivery across multiple office functions.
proposed_markets.economics_risk: Service economics are tied to labor-enabled administrative delivery, process standardization, client scope, and responsibility for execution of routine office workflows; complete operational takeover is excluded.
explicit_exclusions: Complete operation of a client's business
Standalone accounting, payroll, tax, document, mail, IT, legal, or other single support service
Internal corporate, subsidiary, or regional managing offices
proposed_markets.job_to_be_done: Run a client's recurring day-to-day office administration as an integrated external service.
proposed_markets.workforce_model: Administrative personnel organized to execute multiple routine office functions for clients; not the operating staff for the client's entire business.
